units.source: Custom share template
This topic of creating share templates is considered advanced and requires JavaScript/EJS knowledge.
The default share template should cover most normal uses.
For full control over the HTML structure of a shared page — beyond what custom CSS, JS, or HTML snippets allow — you can replace the page template entirely using the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ relation.
To do so:
Create a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Code__TRILIUM_PH_1__ note with the language __TRILIUM_PH_2__Embedded JavaScript__TRILIUM_PH_3__ (EJS).

For a shared note to apply the newly created template, apply the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ relation pointing to the note created at step (1). Make use of __TRILIUM_PH_1__Attribute Inheritance__TRILIUM_PH_2__ to apply it to multiple shared notes.
There are two important constraints to be aware of:

Because EJS templates execute arbitrary server-side JavaScript, __TRILIUM_PH_0__ only takes effect when backend scripting is enabled. If it is disabled (see __TRILIUM_PH_1__Security__TRILIUM_PH_2__), the relation is ignored and the default template is used. For the same reason, __TRILIUM_PH_3__only apply templates from notes you trust__TRILIUM_PH_4__.

The template note must be part of the shared subtree (just like __TRILIUM_PH_0__, __TRILIUM_PH_1__) in order for it to be loaded. To prevent it from being shown in the navigation, apply __TRILIUM_PH_2__ to it.

units.source: Available variables__TRILIUM_PH_0__
Your template is rendered with a context object exposing the note and its rendering environment. The most useful values are:
Variable
Description
The note being rendered. Use it to read attributes (__TRILIUM_PH_0__), __TRILIUM_PH_1__, child notes, etc.
The note's already-rendered HTML content, as a string.
Extra HTML to place in the document head for this note (used by some note types).
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ when the note has no content of its own.

The values of the page's __TRILIUM_PH_0__: __TRILIUM_PH_1__ (the note's title, followed by the site's), __TRILIUM_PH_2__ (__TRILIUM_PH_3__), __TRILIUM_PH_4__ (__TRILIUM_PH_5__) and __TRILIUM_PH_6__ with __TRILIUM_PH_7__, __TRILIUM_PH_8__, __TRILIUM_PH_9__, __TRILIUM_PH_10__ and __TRILIUM_PH_11__ (__TRILIUM_PH_12__ with an image, __TRILIUM_PH_13__ without). A value whose label is not set is __TRILIUM_PH_14__. __TRILIUM_PH_15__ lists the description, OpenGraph and Twitter __TRILIUM_PH_16__ tags of the values that are set, each with __TRILIUM_PH_17__ (__TRILIUM_PH_18__ or __TRILIUM_PH_19__), __TRILIUM_PH_20__ and __TRILIUM_PH_21__.

The site logo above the navigation tree and, on a narrow screen, in the header: __TRILIUM_PH_0__ (__TRILIUM_PH_1__, otherwise the site's root page), __TRILIUM_PH_2__ (the __TRILIUM_PH_3__ image, or __TRILIUM_PH_4__), __TRILIUM_PH_5__ (the icon classes of the site's root note, shown when there is no __TRILIUM_PH_6__), and __TRILIUM_PH_7__ and __TRILIUM_PH_8__ for the image.

The navigation tree of the site: its visible pages, each with __TRILIUM_PH_0__, __TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__, __TRILIUM_PH_3__, __TRILIUM_PH_4__, __TRILIUM_PH_5__ (the page being shown), __TRILIUM_PH_6__ (that page or one of its ancestors) and __TRILIUM_PH_7__.

The classes of the content element: __TRILIUM_PH_0__, __TRILIUM_PH_1__ for text and Markdown notes, __TRILIUM_PH_2__ for a note that takes the whole page (such as a PDF, a web view, a calendar, a geo map or an image), and __TRILIUM_PH_3__ when the note has no content of its own.

The links to the note's visible children, each with __TRILIUM_PH_0__, __TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__, __TRILIUM_PH_3__, __TRILIUM_PH_4__ (its icon classes), __TRILIUM_PH_5__ (its __TRILIUM_PH_6__ or the start of its text, with a line break between paragraphs, or __TRILIUM_PH_7__) and __TRILIUM_PH_8__ (when it has no excerpt, its first ten visible children, each with __TRILIUM_PH_9__, __TRILIUM_PH_10__, __TRILIUM_PH_11__ and __TRILIUM_PH_12__). Empty for a note that is not a collection, a text note or a code note, for a note that takes the whole page, and with __TRILIUM_PH_13__.
How the default template lays __TRILIUM_PH_0__ out: __TRILIUM_PH_1__ for a collection whose view type is list, __TRILIUM_PH_2__ otherwise.

The pages before and after the note in the navigation tree, as __TRILIUM_PH_0__ and __TRILIUM_PH_1__, each with __TRILIUM_PH_2__ and __TRILIUM_PH_3__, or __TRILIUM_PH_4__. Both __TRILIUM_PH_5__ for a note that takes the whole page.

The languages of the page: __TRILIUM_PH_0__ with the __TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__ of the application's language, and __TRILIUM_PH_3__ with those of the note's content language, or __TRILIUM_PH_4__ when they are the same.

When the note was last changed, as __TRILIUM_PH_0__ for a __TRILIUM_PH_1__ element and as __TRILIUM_PH_2__ in the application's language, or __TRILIUM_PH_3__, which it also is for a note that takes the whole page.
Whether the default template shows the note's title above the content. Always __TRILIUM_PH_0__.
The icon classes of the note, which the default template shows beside the title in a row of its own for a note that takes the whole page; __TRILIUM_PH_0__ for any other note.
The HTML of the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ snippets for each location, such as __TRILIUM_PH_1__. Every location is present, empty when no snippet goes there.
The root of the shared subtree as __TRILIUM_PH_0__ — handy for a site-wide title or logo.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ / __TRILIUM_PH_1__
Arrays of stylesheet / script URLs the default theme would inject (includes anything added via __TRILIUM_PH_0__ / __TRILIUM_PH_1__).
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ / __TRILIUM_PH_1__
Resolved favicon and logo URLs. Without __TRILIUM_PH_0__, __TRILIUM_PH_1__ is the Trilium logo.

The icon fonts to preload, each with __TRILIUM_PH_0__ and __TRILIUM_PH_1__ (the font's media type): Boxicons, and the icon packs used by the logo, the navigation tree or the subpages. The default template adds a __TRILIUM_PH_2__ for each, so that the icons do not appear only after the first paint.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ during a static HTML export, __TRILIUM_PH_1__ for a live server render.

Error handling__TRILIUM_PH_0__
If your template throws an error while rendering, Trilium logs the error and quietly falls back to the default template, so a broken template never takes the shared page down.
